Probabilistic modeling of wind energy potential for power grid
expansion planning
Gyeongmin Kim, Jin Hur *
Department of Climate and Energy Systems Engineering, Ewha Womans University, Republic of Korea
article info
Article history:
Received 15 May 2020
Received in revised form
29 April 2021
Accepted 1 May 2021
Available online 6 May 2021
Keywords:
Wind energy potential
Probabilistic model
Weibull distribution
Monte Carlo simulation
Capacity factor
Grid expansion planning
abstract
The increasing integration of wind energy generation into energy systems has led to dif ﬁculties in power
ﬂow calculations due to uncertainty and variability, which signi ﬁcantly affect the stability and reliability
of power grids. Consequently, it is critical to evaluate the energy security limit of power grids based on
probabilistic approaches. In this paper, we propose the probabilistic modeling of wind energy potential
for power grid expansion planning. The proposed probabilistic model estimates wind energy potential
through Weibull distribution, Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS), and the enhanced spatial modeling based
on universal kriging. It can be used to establish the expansion plan for transmission and distribution
facilities to resolve the variability and uncertainty issues of wind generation resources, which is expected
to increase the penetration levels of renewable energy. To validate the proposed model, the empirical
data from the Jeju Island's wind farms are considered in South Korea.

1. Introduction
The percentage of renewable energy and renewable energy
policies of each country are increasing due to the obligation to
reduce greenhouse gas emissions according to the Paris Climate
Change Accord, and the agreement to deplete fossil fuel [ 1]. Ac-
cording to Ref. [ 2], CO 2 emission is expected to increase by 2.2%
annually by 2020, and existing fossil fuels such as oil and natural
gas cause environmental pollution problems such as ozone layer
depletion and climate change [ 3]. On the other hand, renewable
energy sources are unlimited clean energy which emit none or very
little amounts of air pollutants and greenhouse gases, e.g. solar
energy, wind energy, biomass energy, hydropower, etc [ 2,4].
In 2018, renewable energy generation exceeded 33% of the
global power capacity. Fig. 1 shows the percentage of estimated
renewable energy share in global electricity production [ 5]. From
2017 to 2018, global renewable energy generation increased by
approximately 14.5% from 2166.5 to 2480.4 TWh, respectively, and
has changed primarily from solar and wind. During the same time
period, the United States and Germany increased solar power by
approximately 24.4% from 78.1 to 97.1 TWh and 17.2% from
39.4 TWh ( ’17) to 46.2 TWh, respectively, while France increased
wind power by 15.8% from 24.3 to 28.2 TWh, respectively [ 6].
According to the 8th Basic Plan for Long-term Electricity Supply
and Demand, the Republic of Korea aims to achieve 20% (132 TWh)
of renewable energy generation by 2030. Considering the stability
of the power system and the potential of renewable energy, the
target for renewable energy power generation was set at 20%, while
the amount of renewable energy capacity newly supplied by 2030
should be 48.7 GW. Fig. 2 shows the Republic of Korea's Renewable
Energy 2016e2030 Implementation Plan.
“Carbon Free Island Jeju by 2030 ” is a project to achieve Korea's
decarbonization and renewable energy generation goals, and aims
to install 2350 MW of Jeju's onshore and offshore wind farm by
2030. Due to the geographical characteristics of Jeju Island, instal-
lation of offshore wind farm is more suitable than onshore, and if
the conditions for offshore wind are well established, offshore wind
farm has the advantage of higher electricity production than
onshore [ 7]. We need to estimate wind energy potential and
analyze power system operational ef ﬁciency before installing new
offshore wind farms to achieve the Carbon Free Island goal, and it is
necessary to consider transmission expansion plans according to
the increase in HVDC and offshore wind farms [ 8e10]. China has
expanded the capacity of wind power, but there is a problem of
curtailment due to transmission inadequacy and minimum gener-
ation limits [ 11]. In addition, high penetration above 20 e30% of* Corresponding author.

installed capacity cause system security problems [ 12e14].
Renewable energy sources centered on solar and wind power have
problems of uncertainty and variability [ 15,16]. Speci ﬁcally, wind
power generation resources have greater variability because they
are affected by weather factors such as temperature, wind speed
and direction [ 17]. Wind power output is variable, although sta-
tistical patterns can be identi ﬁed over a long period of time [ 18].
Therefore, in order to secure system reliability against high pene-
tration of wind power generation, it is necessary to improve the
existing power grid system analysis and probabilistic prediction
techniques of renewable energy output or to develop new power
generation methods [ 19e22]. In compliance with the criteria for
expanding and stabilizing power systems, as well as ef ﬁcient uti-
lization of existing infrastructure or planning to expand the grid
capacity as per the expansion of renewable energy, should be
considered [23].
The Republic of Korea established a transmission system plan
based on the Ministry of Trade, Industry, and Energy's Power Sys-
tem Reliability and Electrical Quality Maintenance Standards and is
currently conducting continuous system reinforcement and
expansion essential to maintain the power system reliability [ 24].
In many European countries, the rapid expansion of renewable
energy has created a need to expand the grid [ 25]. In the future,
long-term energy system modeling is required to secure high
penetration of Renewable Energy and system reliability [ 26,27],
and there is increasing awareness of the need to study grid
expansion plans [ 28].
In this paper, we propose the probabilistic modeling of wind
energy potential for power grid expansion planning. We analyzed
the probabilistic model based on a Weibull distribution and Monte
Carlo simulations using the measured data of existing wind farms
and the estimated potential capacity of wind power resources on
Jeju Island, Korea, through the enhanced spatial modeling with
universal kriging. The proposed algorithm will be a key a role to
estimate the potential of wind generating resources for all spatio-
temporal scales, and will be used to select the optimal location for
new wind farm candidate sites through wind resource potential
estimation. In addition, it can be applied to the establishment of a
stable operation plan and expansion plan for transmission and
distribution facilities with high wind power penetrations. The
remainder of this paper is organized as follows. Section 2 presents
the probabilistic modeling for estimating wind energy potential for
new farm locations. In Section 3, the proposed probabilistic
modeling of wind energy potential for power grid expansion
planning is discussed. We present the probabilistic scenarios to use
with the modeled wind power outputs, which re ﬂects the Island's
seasonal conditions, for the empirically modeled power grid for
Jeju Island. Finally, conclusions are presented in Section 4.
2. Probabilistic modeling for estimating wind energy
potential
In this section, the capacity factor [ 32] calculated from the wind
farm output data ﬁts a two-parameter Weibull distribution with
shape ( k) and scale ( c
), and we used the energy pattern method
(EPM) [29e31] to calculate the two parameters. Sampled data were
extracted from the results of the Monte Carlo simulations to
calculate the scale and shape parameters. The 95% con ﬁdence in-
tervals of the sample data were used to estimate the capacity of the
new wind farm target points through universal kriging.
2.1. Probabilistic modeling based on Monte Carlo Simulation
Before the Monte Carlo simulation, the R program was used to
select the probability distribution model suitable for the capacity
factor data of the wind farm. Using a histogram of the Monte Carlo
simulation results, the optimal probability model with the lowest
Bayesian information criterion value was selected, and the appli-
cability of the probability model was veri ﬁed. Monte Carlo simu-
lation is a method of random sampling based on parameters
extracted by probability ﬁtting of measured data. It is used to model
the uncertainty of system elements and to evaluate the probabi-
listic steady-state stability of the power system [ 33].
We used a Weibull distribution function with two parameters,
namely shape and scale, for wind power estimation [ 29]. In this
section, the capacity factor was applied to the 2-parameter Weibull
distribution function. The Weibull distribution function is

3. Estimation of wind energy potential for power grid
expansion planning
The capacity factors of eight wind farms on Jeju Island were
calculated using 2017's 1-h unit wind power data clustered over the
four seasons to analyze the probability models. Wind farm location
data such as latitude and longitude were used to perform spatial
modeling based on the probability distribution calculated via the
Weibull distribution and Monte Carlo simulations. Fig. 3 shows the
location of each wind farm on Jeju Island. In this ﬁgure, capital
letters in white are existing points of wind farms and lower-case in
grey are target points.
Before estimating the potential of wind energy through proba-
bilistic modeling, the wind outputs data were preprocessed as ca-
pacity factors, and the capacity factor patterns of each wind power
plant in Jeju were analyzed. South Korea is located in a
temperateeclimate zone in the mid elatitudes, with four distinct
seasons (spring, summer, fall, and winter), and Jeju Island is a
volcanic island that has stronger wind than inland South Korea.
Wind speed has a high correlation with wind power output, and if
the geographical characteristics of Jeju Island are considered, the
wind power output is expected to be highest in winter. As a result of
analysis through case study, the wind power capacity factor was
highest in winter and lowest in summer. Fig. 4 shows the seasonal
wind power capacity factor pattern.
Fig. 5 shows the proposed probabilistic model to estimate wind
energy potential for power grid expansion planning. As shown in
Fig. 5 , the potential capacity factors for new wind farm locations
can be determined by the proposed probabilistic model. The algo-
rithm consists of four steps, and the contents of each step are as
follows. Step 1 is the process of calculating the wind power capacity
factor based on wind power outputs and installed capacity, and
analyzing the characteristics of wind power data. In this paper, data
for each wind farm were analyzed by EPM and two-parameter
weibull distribution. Step 2 is the probabilistic modeling process.
Monte carlo simulations were performed based on the Weibull
distribution parameters calculated for each wind farm. The
maximum and minimum values of the 95% con ﬁdence interval of
the extracted sampling data are used as input data to perform the
universal kriging of step 3. In step 3, universal kriging was per-
formed based on the data of eight existing wind farms, and the
proposed model was veri ﬁed through cross-validation. In step 4,
the potential capacity factor is estimated using the location (lati-
tude and longitude) data of Jeju new wind farms for universal
kriging. The estimated data is used as a renewable energy genera-
tion input scenario of the practical power system, and power grid
expansion planning can be established through the analysis of
power system elements such as branch ﬂow and bus voltage.

Cross-validation assumes that one of the existing eight wind
farms does not know wind farm capacity factor, and performs

Cross-validation is performed on eight wind farms. To analyze the
cross-validation result, the 95% conﬁdence interval of the measured
and predicted data through universal kriging were compared. The
prediction error of the measured and predicted data for each wind
farm was calculated through RMSE. As a result of the prediction, it
was con ﬁrmed that the wind farm capacity factor prediction was
performed well through universal kriging.
The reliability of the model estimation results was veriﬁed using
cross-validation. The capacity factor of the new wind farm was
estimated using the probabilistic model. The location of the new
wind farm was set as the point where the wind resources were
expected to be high [ 43]. Table 4 reports the potential capacity
factor of the area calculated through universal kriging. A table of
values means the estimated capacity factor of the new wind farm at
the 95% con ﬁdence interval. Fig. 8 shows estimates of the capacity
factor of the new wind farm C for different seasons. In this ﬁgure,
red lines are the means and blue lines are 95% con ﬁdence intervals.
3.3. Application of the proposed methodology
The proposed probabilistic modeling algorithm for estimating
wind energy potential can be applied to all spatiotemporal scales.
Table 5 shows the pseudocode of the proposed algorithm. The
measured wind power outputs and installed capacity of wind farms
are used to estimate the capacity factor of the new wind farm. The
algorithm consists of two steps, the ﬁrst step is probabilistic
modeling, and the second step is power system security analysis.
In this paper, the Weibull distribution, which is the most suit-
able probability model for wind power output characteristics, was
selected as the ﬁtting model. The proposed algorithm can be
applied to other cases with different characteristics if the data is
mounted on an appropriate probability model according to the
characteristics of the data to be used by the user as well as the wind
power data.

3.4. Case studies: power grid expansion planning in Jeju Island's
systems
The 2030 Jeju power grid was modeled using the capacity factor
and 95% conﬁdence intervals of the target points extracted through
probabilistic modeling. The predicted data of peak power demand
and power generation, excluding wind power, were the inputs, and
the base case and two scenarios were set for the analysis of line
overload and power grid expansion planning. Scenario 1 expanded
the line capacity by the overload rate for lines with a load overload
rate of 100% or higher than the base case, and inputs were the 95%
conﬁdence intervals of nine new wind farms estimated through
probabilistic modeling. In Scenario 2, the capacity of the line with
an overload rate of 80% or more of the base case was expanded by
the overload rate, and the power generation of the new wind farms
were the same as in Scenario 1. Table 6 reports the line overload for
each scenario.
Fig. 9 is the base case for Jeju's power grid. There is a total of
eight lines where overload occurs; ﬁve have a line overload rate of
150%, and three have a line overload rate within the 100% e150%
interval. In addition, there are four potential overloads (over 80% of
the line overload rate). Fig. 10 shows the power simulation results
of Scenarios 1 and 2 with 95% con ﬁdence intervals of the nine wind
farm target points estimated in this paper. For Scenario 1, there
were no lines with an overload rate exceeding 100%, nine lines with
an overload rate of within the 80%e100% were analyzed. In the case
of Scenario 2, there were no lines with an overload rate exceeding
100%, three lines with an overload rate of within the 80% e100%
were analyzed.
As a result, Scenario 2 was more relieved of line overload on a
base case than Scenario 1. To analysis power system security, pre-
dict the power generation of new wind farms and put them into the

4. Conclusions
The increasing integration of wind energy generation into en-
ergy systems has led to difﬁculties in power ﬂow calculations due to
uncertainty and variability, which signi ﬁcantly affect the stability
and reliability of power grids. In this paper, we propose the prob-
abilistic modeling of wind energy potential for power grid expan-
sion planning. The probabilistic models that considered the
correlations of wind farms were implemented using wind power
output data from Jeju Island, Korea, and the capacity factors of wind
farms were estimated. To estimate the capacity factor of the new
wind farm through universal kriging, power output data from Jeju
Island's wind farms were calculated as capacity factors, and 95%
conﬁdence intervals and means were sampled by seasonal Weilbull
distribution and Monte Carlo simulations. To perform Monte Carlo
simulations, the optimal probability model with the lowest BIC was
selected, and each parameter ( k, c) of the Weibull distribution was
calculated through the EPM. Sampling data from probability
models were used for spatial modeling, and universal kriging was
performed by applying a variogram based on the spherical model
and speciﬁc parameters considering the existing wind farms. Cross-
validation was performed to estimate the capacity factors of the
new wind farm loctions and to verify the reliability of the model's
estimated results. Cross-validation results were quantitatively
evaluated using RMSE through universal kriging. Based on the
estimated capacity factors of the target points calculated using the
Kriging technique, we analyzed the potential of wind resources
through system analysis and formulated the power grid expansion
plan. As we discussed in previous sections, the wind energy po-
tential estimation is needed to select the optimal location for new
wind farm candidate sites. The potential capacity factors of wind
generating resources at the target location can be applied to the
calculation of operational reserves for enhancing the power system
reliability and power grid expansion planning for high wind power
penetrations.
In future, we will use the proposed algorithm to create the
probabilistic renewable energy penetration scenarios, and will
deploy it to enhance the security of power grids.
